summary: This short biographical note covers the career of Ercole Bernabei, a musician born in Caprarola who studied with Orazio Benevoli in Rome. It traces his posts as organist at San Luigi dei Francesi from 1653, as maestro di cappella at the Archbasilica of St. John Lateran from July 1665, and at the Cappella Giulia in St. Peter's Basilica from 1672 to 1674 under the protection of Christina, Queen of Sweden.
one_line: Biographical note on Ercole Bernabei, a Caprarola-born musician whose Roman church posts ran from San Luigi dei Francesi to St. Peter's Basilica.
key_facts: Ercole Bernabei was born in Caprarola.
Ercole Bernabei became a pupil of Orazio Benevoli in Rome.
From 1653, Ercole Bernabei served as organist at San Luigi dei Francesi.
Ercole Bernabei succeeded Luigi Rossi as organist at San Luigi dei Francesi.
In July 1665, Ercole Bernabei was appointed "maestro di cappella" at the Archbasilica of St. John Lateran.
From 1672 to 1674, Ercole Bernabei held the post of maestro di cappella at the Cappella Giulia in St. Peter's Basilica.
Ercole Bernabei obtained his Cappella Giulia post thanks to the protection of Christina, Queen of Sweden.
